messages:
acme_ops: Hey team — after we migrated the private deployment into our corporate VPC, our app can't talk to the private control plane. All calls to https://private-api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health fail with either "connect timeout" or a TLS handshake error. We think this started after ops rolled out a new outbound gateway.

acme_ops: Quick repro:
```
$ curl -v https://private-api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
* Connected to proxy.corp.internal (10.10.10.5) port 8080 (#0)
* Establish HTTP proxy tunnel to private-api.redwood-inference.com:443
* TLS handshake failed: ssl: TLSv1.3 handshake failure
* Closing connection 0
curl: (35) TLS handshake failed
```

acme_ops: If we run the same curl from a host on a different network that bypasses the gateway it works.

kevin_support: Thanks — looks like outbound gateway is doing something to the TLS. Can you paste the output of `openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername private-api.redwood-inference.com` from a failing host (one behind the gateway)? That will show cert details / SNI.

acme_ops: Pasted below (redacted):
```
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=1 C = US, O = Corp Proxy, CN = corp-proxy-ca
verify return:1
---
Certificate chain
 0 s:/CN=proxy.corp.internal
   i:/C=US/O=Corp Proxy/CN=corp-proxy-ca
---
Server certificate
subject=/CN=proxy.corp.internal
issuer=/C=US/O=Corp Proxy/CN=corp-proxy-ca
---
SSL handshake has read 3425 bytes and written 1372 bytes
---
```

acme_ops: So the proxy is terminating TLS and presenting its own cert (Corp Proxy CA). But our client expects Redwood cert and fails verification (we don't have corp CA installed on our runtime container). Also we're seeing intermittent 403s from the control plane when requests get through.

anjali_networks: Two things likely going on:
- Your proxy is doing TLS MITM (inspect) and replacing certs -> you need the proxy CA in your container/system trust store or configure the proxy to not inspect traffic to private-api.redwood-inference.com
- If the proxy rewrites Host/SNI or strips HTTP CONNECT semantics, the control plane may see mismatched SNI/Host header -> that explains 403s (request authenticated to wrong hostname)

devon_infra: Can you also run a tcpdump on the client to capture the initial TLS ClientHello? We want to verify what SNI is being sent and whether the proxy modifies it.

acme_ops: tcpdump snippet (client side):
```
12:12:03.123456 IP client -> proxy TCP 60
12:12:03.123999 TLS Client Hello, SNI: private-api.redwood-inference.com
```

acme_ops: And on the proxy frontend we see Client Hello SNI rewritten to "proxy.corp.internal" in the TLS session to the backend.

lisa_devex: OK that's consistent. Two remediation paths:
1) Allow TLS passthrough for private-api.redwood-inference.com on the gateway (no inspect, just CONNECT) — preferred for private control planes.
2) If you must inspect, install the corporate proxy root CA inside the app/container OS trust store so verification succeeds, and ensure the proxy preserves original SNI/Host headers when proxying.

kevin_support: Workarounds on your side while we coordinate with your network team:
- Add an explicit NO_PROXY/NO_PROXY_HOSTS entry for private-api.redwood-inference.com on the hosts/containers that talk to Redwood.
- Alternatively set REDWOOD_API_URL to use the IP address (not ideal) and add the IP to proxy bypass. Note: if using IP, ensure certificate validation still works (SNI mismatch then occurs).

anjali_networks: Also check the allowlist — some corporate egress gateways only allow outbound to specific IPs/domains. Please add the following FQDNs to the egress allowlist and permit CONNECT/443 without TLS inspection:
- private-api.redwood-inference.com
- control-plane.redwood-inference.com
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com

kevin_support: Please run these tests and share results:
1) curl with proxy auth verbose:
```
curl -v --proxy http://proxy.corp.internal:8080 https://private-api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
```
2) openssl s_client to proxy and direct (compare):
```
openssl s_client -connect proxy.corp.internal:8080 -servername private-api.redwood-inference.com
openssl s_client -connect private-api.redwood-inference.com:443 -servername private-api.redwood-inference.com
```
3) if you're using containers, confirm container image has corp CA in /etc/ssl/certs or update image.

acme_ops: Ran the tests. Confirmed curl via proxy returns 407 if proxy auth missing; with creds we get MITM cert and TLS handshake succeeds but application-level validation fails. Direct connect works.

acme_ops: We added NO_PROXY for the host on the app container and asked network to pass-through. After that health checks succeed.

kevin_support: Great — sounds like pass-through fixed it. For long term:
- Ask network to whitelist the FQDNs above for CONNECT 443 passthrough OR
- Provide corp-proxy CA to your runtime (k8s image or node) and ensure proxy preserves SNI and Host header
- If you're using a private deployment with pinned certificate expectations, prefer passthrough so no cert substitution occurs

support-bot: Created support ticket SR-4321 for the allowlist + CA guidance. Linking convo to the Customer Success case.

acme_ops: Thanks everyone. We'll keep pass-through in place for now and will follow up with network to finalise allowlist + CA distribution. Closing from our side once network confirms.

devon_infra: Noted — leaving a remediation doc in onboarding repo about "egress gateway TLS inspection and Redwood private control planes" with the commands we used.

lisa_devex: Adding a short blurb in the Private deployment README: "If your org performs TLS inspection, either enable passthrough for Redwood control plane FQDNs or install the inspection CA into your runtime images." :+1:

acme_ops: Network confirmed allowlist and passthrough configured at 2023-11-17T15:40Z. All green. Last check:
```
curl -v https://private-api.redwood-inference.com/v1/health
* Connected to private-api.redwood-inference.com (198.51.100.42) port 443 (#0)
* TLS handshaking completed with server certificate issued to private-api.redwood-inference.com
{"status":"ok"}
```

acme_ops: Marking resolved.
